headline: Agentic AI is a loop, not a menu
lede: RAG, agents, MCP, and A2A are layers. Skills and rules shape behavior. Most teams need fewer layers than the pitch deck suggests; start at the thinnest layer that solves the job.

source.method: hand-extracted from the published card; text is the card's text

layers.job: Knowledge — ground answers in your docs
Control loop — plan, act, observe, stop

decisions.problem: Answers ignore our docs, go stale, or invent policy
decisions.example: Internal policy bot cites the latest refund SOP; use GraphRAG when the question is about how entities link

decisions.problem: Need live reads or writes against systems — not a stale index
decisions.example: Stock check hits ERP now; same agent opens a Jira bug with logs after a failed deploy

decisions.problem: Only 1–2 APIs inside one app; no reuse yet
decisions.example: One Flask service calling Stripe + SendGrid; move to MCP when those same tools must serve multiple apps

decisions.problem: Fixed path with a model in one or two slots
decisions.example: Invoice PDF → extract fields → validate → post to ledger; model fills gaps, code owns order

decisions.problem: Multi-step work that branches, retries, and must stop cleanly
decisions.example: Month-end expense pack: pull receipts, match policy via RAG, flag outliers, wait for Approve
“Never push main; always cite sources; Finnish UI copy stays formal” in every session

decisions.problem: Named playbook with steps and a verify gate
decisions.example: “Author a Power BI page” skill: open model, place visuals, validate PBIR, screenshot check

decisions.problem: Money, prod, or irreversible writes in the path
decisions.example: Refund > €50 pauses for Approve; step and spend caps stop a runaway loop

decisions.problem: Tone/format still wrong after prompts + RAG
decisions.example: Bank chat must stick to a fixed compliance template; keep changing facts in retrieval, not weights

decisions.problem: Specialist agents owned by different teams or vendors
decisions.example: Support agent hands a refund packet to Finance-ops across two tenants; each agent keeps its own MCP tools

decisions.problem: Don’t know if the system still works after a change
decisions.example: 20 golden tickets; block ship if pass rate drops; inspect the tool path when a case fails

buildOrder: Default build order: prompted chat → RAG → one agent with tools/MCP → stateful workflow + human gate → multi-agent inside one framework → A2A only when ownership boundaries are real.

behavior.title: Rules · standing orders
behavior.body: Always on or path-scoped. Safety, voice, repo law. Keep short. Cursor: .cursor/rules, AGENTS.md.

behavior.title: Skills · runbooks
behavior.body: Load when the task matches. Multi-step + verify. Cursor: SKILL.md. Don’t wrap one API call as a skill.

behavior.title: Memory check
behavior.body: LLM = language. RAG = library. MCP = hands. Rules = standing orders. Skills = runbooks.

killSwitch: Max steps, max €/tokens, tool allowlist. If you can’t stop it, you don’t ship it.
antiPatterns: Agent for pure Q&A (start with RAG)
Treating MCP and RAG as either/or
Fine-tuning for facts that change weekly
Unbounded autonomy where money or prod moves
Tools without schemas, budgets, or kill switches
Always-on rules that belong in a skill

alwaysOn.label: Security
alwaysOn.body: Tool allowlist, spend and step caps

alwaysOn.label: Governance
alwaysOn.body: Who owns policy and the audit trail

alwaysOn.label: Observability
alwaysOn.body: Traces and the tool path when a case fails
